parsed.summary: Lean asserts two existence results about finitely generated, countable groups in Type 0 that are ICC and have Kazhdan property (T). (1) There are two non-isomorphic such groups Γ, Λ whose group von Neumann algebras admit a normal, trace-preserving *-isomorphism. (2) There are Λ and a sequence Γ_n of such groups, with Λ and all Γ_n pairwise non-isomorphic and all their group factors tracially isomorphic. The definitions of ICC, property (T), the left regular representation, L(G) (as a double commutant) and the canonical trace are faithful. The factor-isomorphism notion adds normality and trace-preservation, which only strengthens the existence claim. The main caveat is coverage: the 'Moreover' part of Theorem 1.2 (finite-index embeddings Γ_0 ↪ Γ_n of index 2^{4n}, commensurability) is not formalized.

glossary.standard_concept: unitary representation of a discrete group
glossary.note: No continuity is needed for discrete groups.

glossary.plain: For every finite K ⊆ G and every ε > 0 there is a unit vector ξ with ‖π(g)ξ − ξ‖ < ε for all g ∈ K.
Every unitary representation of G on a Hilbert space in the same universe that has almost invariant unit vectors has a nonzero invariant vector.
glossary.note: Only Hilbert spaces in Type 0 are quantified. For a countable group this is equivalent to the standard notion, since separable representations suffice.

glossary.plain: The *-isomorphism and its inverse preserve suprema of arbitrary families of projections.
glossary.note: Automatic for *-isomorphisms of von Neumann algebras, so it is an extra but satisfiable requirement.

glossary.standard_concept: isomorphism of group von Neumann algebras
glossary.note: Stronger than a bare isomorphism. For II1 factors trace preservation is automatic by uniqueness of the trace.

lean_claims.plain: There exist countable groups Γ, Λ with the following properties: both finitely generated, both ICC, both with property (T); a normal trace-preserving *-isomorphism L(Γ) ≅ L(Λ) exists; and Γ ≇ Λ.

There exist countable groups Λ and Γ_0, Γ_1, … with the following properties: all finitely generated, ICC, with property (T); L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ) and L(Γ_m) ≅ L(Γ_n) tracially for all m, n; Γ_m ≇ Γ_n for m ≠ n; and Λ ≇ Γ_n for all n.

paper_claims.plain: There exist finitely generated ICC property-(T) groups Λ, Γ_0, Γ_1, … that are pairwise nonisomorphic with L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ). Moreover, Γ_n contains a subgroup isomorphic to Γ_0 of index 2^{4n}, so the Γ_n are commensurable.
The pair Λ, Γ_0 consists of non-isomorphic ICC property-(T) groups with isomorphic group factors.

coverage.why: Lean additionally demands normality and trace preservation, which are automatic for II1 factors.
Pairwise non-isomorphism and isomorphic factors are captured; the extra Γ_m–Γ_n factor isomorphisms follow by composition.
No subgroup or index statement appears in Lean.

flags.explanation: The isomorphism is required to be normal (preserve projection suprema) and trace-preserving. The paper only says L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ). This is an extra requirement inside an existential, so Lean is stronger.
Property (T) quantifies only over Hilbert spaces in Type 0. This is equivalent to the standard definition for countable groups, since separable representations suffice.
